evidence: Cic. de Orat. 1.177: jūs obscūrum et ignōtum patefacere et illūstrāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly to light up; then to make clear, to set a speech off with ornament, and to make famous (Lewis & Short). Cicero uses it of setting out Greek philosophy in Latin.
To make evident; also, in public law, to proclaim someone elected (cōnsulem dēclārāre, Cic. Mur. 2): Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: philosophiamque veterem illam ā Sōcrate ortam Latīnīs litterīs illūstrāre
phrases.english: and to set out clearly in Latin that old philosophy which sprang from Socrates

illustro.html: From illūstris, of the family of lūx: de Vaan 355, s.v. lūx, illūstris “bright, famous”.

sources: Lewis & Short: illustro · Lewis & Short: declaro
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 355.
